solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Right to quit dream about large loch — here's wake-up call

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened dream goes round the two letters
to quit means to leave, so the letter for right departs from the word for a dream

parts.note: a reverie is a daydream
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
L is the map abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: Someone is roused from a dream of a big Scottish lake by an early-morning call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to quit' takes the second R out of REVERIE, leaving REVEIE; 'about' wraps that round LL, giving REVEI-LL-E. 'here's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reveille is the bugle signal sounded to rouse soldiers in the morning, a military alarm call.

clue.text: Be unable to prosecute what streaker will do?

definitions.meaning: to lack any evidence against someone, so no case can be brought
a streaker runs about naked, wearing no clothes at all

explanation.surface: A wry question about why a naked runner can't be charged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means lacking incriminating evidence, and read literally it describes being unclothed.

clue.text: A lot of information perhaps turning up about good puzzle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so A MINE goes round the letter for good
in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mine of information is a rich source of facts, so a mine is a lot of information

explanation.surface: A heap of data might suddenly reveal a decent puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts G into A MINE, giving AMGINE; 'turning up' reads that from the bottom, as this is a down entry. 'A lot of' looks like 'most of' but is part of 'a mine of information'.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a riddle or mystery, something baffling to work out.

clue.text: Band upset priest

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters of priest are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A musical group has offended a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a narrow band of colour, as on a flag or a uniform sleeve.

clue.text: Unrealistic place is a real spoof, concocted with a hint of devilment

indicators.note: concocted means cooked up or made up, so these letters are mixed into a new arrangement
a hint of a word is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Something devilish is cooked up as a hoax about a dreamland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hint of' gives D from devilment, which joins the letters of IS A REAL SPOOF before 'concocted' rearranges all thirteen.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a state of happiness built on illusion, an imaginary haven of false hope.

clue.text: Girl, mostly, is smart

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of it, so the word for a girl loses its final letter

parts.note: chick is informal slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: A girl is mostly well turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant, as smart does of dress.

clue.text: Stop having mother in control

indicators.note: in says the word for mother sits inside the word for control

parts.note: to rein is to restrain or control, from a horse's reins
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone stays put because mum is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like an order to halt, but it means stay on, as in stopping at a friend's.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop somewhere can mean to stay there, keeping put rather than leaving.

clue.text: Work hard in attempt for cup

indicators.note: in says the work and hard letters sit inside the attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
op, short for opus, is a work of music
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Toiling away in a bid to win the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup awarded in sport is a prize, the kind of trophy a team lifts.

clue.text: Lady's Equerry's first in attendance

parts.note: her is the possessive for a lady, as in her hat

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A noblewoman's royal attendant is the first to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: An equerry is an officer attending a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present is the sense, as in a roll call answered by someone who is present.

clue.text: Damaged rig, refrigerated, reversing, by end of block — traffic jams result

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so the letters of rig are scrambled
reversing means the word for refrigerated is read backwards

parts.note: refrigerated food is kept cold

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A broken-down chilled lorry backing up near a building causes a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaged' makes GRI from RIG; 'reversing' turns COLD into DLOC; 'end of' gives K from block. 'by' and 'result' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gridlock is total standstill on city roads, when queues of vehicles block every junction.

clue.text: Assign to a cell roughly behind front of Alcatraz

indicators.note: behind says the scrambled letters come after the letter from Alcatraz
the front of a word is its first letter
roughly means approximately or not exactly, so the letters of to a cell are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prisoner is put in a cell at the famous island jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' turns TO A CELL into LLOCATE, which goes after A, the front of Alcatraz.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to give out or allot something to someone, as one would assign a task.

clue.text: Drink a drop? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word for a drop loses its last letter

parts.note: a tear is a single drop of liquid from the eye

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a drink, just a drop, but not a full measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the final R of TEAR. 'a drop' looks like an amount of drink but is the teardrop.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the classic hot beverage brewed from dried leaves.

clue.text: Put lots of people on deck

definitions.meaning: to cram a crowd into a space

explanation.surface: A boat is crammed with passengers on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack a place is to fill it with a crowd, and a pack of cards is a deck.

clue.text: Sleep cut short, leading to obvious bellyache

indicators.note: cut short means losing its end, so the word for sleep drops its final letter

parts.note: a coma is a deep unconscious sleep
plain means clear or obvious

explanation.surface: An unfinished nap leads to a clear stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the last A of COMA. 'bellyache' looks like a stomach pain but is the slang verb; 'leading to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellyache is informal slang for grumbling or moaning about something.

clue.text: Net uses some of Times HTML

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The newspaper's internet pages use some of its web code.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Net uses' as the definition, but 'uses' is a link word: the definition is just 'Net', a noun like the answer. Net here looks like the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesh is netting, a fabric of interlaced threads with gaps between them.

clue.text: Finished with source of mutton, I will have some beef

parts.note: past means over or finished
mutton is the meat of a sheep, and a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A diner has finished the lamb dish and now wants beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of mutton' looks like a first-letter pick but is a sheep; 'will have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, smoked brisket, a cured cut of beef.

clue.text: Difficulty attaching power to lamp

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
a lamp is a light

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to connect electricity to a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A plight is a dangerous or unfortunate situation, a predicament.

clue.text: School is beginning to mask serious divergence of opinions

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A school starts to hide a serious disagreement among staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split within a group, especially a church, caused by differing beliefs.

clue.text: Flaunt error involving South African currency

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the word for error goes round the currency

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a mistake with money from South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is dated British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish is to wave something about showily, displaying it boastfully.

clue.text: Though not first, do better than bottom

indicators.note: not first means the opening letter is removed from the word for doing better

parts.note: to trump is to outdo or beat

explanation.surface: A runner who didn't win still beats the one who came last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not first' drops the T of TRUMP; 'Though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is an animal's hindquarters, a person's backside.

clue.text: Party line repeated term of endearment

parts.note: a do is an informal party

indicators.note: repeated means the letter for line appears twice

explanation.surface: At a party, someone keeps using the same pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: Doll is an affectionate way of addressing someone, like darling or sweetheart.

clue.text: Easy and quiet, containing debate

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the call for quiet surrounds the word for debate

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
to moot is to raise a point for debate, and a moot is a discussion

explanation.surface: A calm, relaxed discussion is held quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth means free of difficulty, as in a smooth ride, an effortless and untroubled process.

clue.text: Bird is featuring in film

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing inside, so is goes within the word for film

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, like skin on custard

explanation.surface: A bird stars in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests a movie but is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch.
